description: §17.1.1 — `else` on a SIBLING element (the legal chain) does NOT fire E-CTRL-005, and `if=` coexisting with `show=` on one element is explicitly legal per §17.1.1's Interaction Notes. Twinned with ctrl-005-else-and-if-same-element-pos: identical structure, the ONLY difference is that `else` sits on a sibling rather than on the `if=` element itself. Doubles as the guard that the E-CTRL-005 check does not over-fire on the legal same-element `if=`+`show=` composition. W-PROGRAM-SPA-INFERRED co-fires incidentally at severity info; not asserted.
rationale: §17.1.1: E-CTRL-005 rejects ONLY the co-occurrence of `else`/`else-if=` with `if=` on a single element. Two distinct rules keep this case silent: (1) `else` on a sibling is the canonical chain form; (2) '`if=`, `else-if=`, and `else` MAY coexist on the same element with `show=`. ... The two attributes compose without conflict.' So a same-element `if=`+`show=` SHALL NOT be rejected. S478 (bootstrap triage C7 / F2): migrated to a twinnable declaration. The legacy inline-typed state-object opener `<session { … }` only declared the cell(s) the chain reads; it is now the legacy declaration `<loggedIn>: bool = false` / `<visible>: bool = true`, which the `scrml fix` §66 rules twin to a §66 declaration (§66.21 row 1). (A direct §66 `let <x:T=v/>` here makes impl#1's ESM client emit throw — "The keyword 'let' is reserved" — so the twinnable legacy declaration keeps both implementations graded.) The if= / else-if= / else chain under test is unchanged.
